title: Amateur radio flashcards: for the FCC General exam (2023–2027 pool)
description: All 423 live questions of the public-domain 2023–2027 General pool, each preceded by the cards that teach what it tests. Builds on the Technician deck.

glossary.ALC: automatic level control, a transmitter circuit that limits audio drive to prevent overmodulation
glossary.AR: the CW procedural signal (prosign) marking the end of a formal message
glossary.BK: the CW procedural signal (prosign) for breaking in to an existing contact
glossary.BPSK31: binary phase-shift keying at PSK31's 31-baud symbol rate
glossary.CB: Citizens Band, a separate radio service with its own frequencies and rules, distinct from amateur radio
glossary.CFR: Code of Federal Regulations (for example, 47 CFR Part 97 holds the amateur radio rules)
glossary.CLOVER: a documented amateur digital data protocol named in 47 CFR 97.309(a)(4)
glossary.DX: distance or distant (telegraphic shorthand); DX stations are distant stations
glossary.EIS: Environmental Impact Statement, as in the pool's fictional "EIS-97" filing option, which the FCC does not actually require
glossary.F1: either the F1 region, the lower part of the ionosphere's F region, or, in an intermodulation formula, an arbitrary label for one of two mixing frequencies (F1, F2)
glossary.F2: the F2 layer, the upper part of the ionosphere’s F region
glossary.FST4: a slow digital mode designed for very weak signals
glossary.G7: Subelement G7, "Practical Circuits" in the General question pool; figure G7-1 is its numbered schematic-symbol key
glossary.IEEE: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
glossary.IF: intermediate frequency, the fixed frequency a receiver's mixer converts signals to before final amplification and detection
glossary.KE1ABC: an example amateur radio call sign used to illustrate the AG indicator
glossary.LISTEN: not a recognised code name; part of the pool's incorrect distractor answer for the Baudot-code question
glossary.MFSK16: multi-frequency-shift keying with 16 tones, a keyboard-to-keyboard digital mode
glossary.MFSK32: a faster variant of MFSK16, a multi-frequency-shift keying digital mode
glossary.MSK144: a minimum-shift keying digital mode designed for meteor-scatter contacts
glossary.PL: as in PL-259, the threaded plug of the UHF connector family
glossary.PN: positive-negative, as in a PN-junction diode formed where P-type and N-type semiconductor meet
glossary.QPSK31: quadrature (four-phase) phase-shift keying at PSK31's 31-baud symbol rate, adding forward error correction
glossary.QRL: Q signal: is this frequency busy?
glossary.QRZ: Q signal: who is calling me?
glossary.QSO: Q signal: I can communicate with … direct; amateurs use it for a contact
glossary.QSY: Q signal: change to transmission on another frequency
glossary.QTC: Q signal: I have … messages for you
glossary.RJ: Registered Jack, as in the RJ-45 telecommunications connector
glossary.S3: a reading of 3 on the S meter, a weak-signal reading
glossary.S8: a reading of 8 on the S meter, one S unit below S9
glossary.S9: a reading of 9 on the S meter, a conventional strong-signal reference point
glossary.SC: suppressed carrier, as in SSB-SC (single sideband with suppressed carrier)
glossary.SELCAL: Selective Calling, a coded tone system that alerts one specific station without constant monitoring; it is not part of Baudot code, despite the pool's wrong-answer option naming it alongside Baudot
glossary.SK: the CW procedural signal (prosign) marking the end of a contact
glossary.SSID: Secondary Station Identifier, a numeric suffix on a packet-radio call sign used to distinguish multiple stations or sessions
glossary.SSTV: slow-scan television, a mode for sending still images over a voice-bandwidth radio channel
glossary.TOR: as in G-TOR, a documented amateur digital data protocol named in 47 CFR 97.309(a)(4)
glossary.W5YI: W5YI-VEC, one of the FCC-recognised volunteer examiner coordinators

notice: Questions from the 2023–2027 General Class (Element 3) question pool, released into the public domain by the NCVEC Question Pool Committee. This deck is independent and is not affiliated with, sponsored, endorsed or approved by the NCVEC, the FCC or any Volunteer Examiner Coordinator.

changelog.notes: First draft, not yet released. The pool is valid until 30 June 2027.

checks.what: Three independent audits read all 1054 cards against the 2023–2027 General pool, 47 CFR Parts 1 and 97 (as amended February 2026), NOAA SWPC and the Navy NEETS manuals, for accuracy and for plain language
checks.result: All 423 pool questions are verbatim with the correct key; two cards missing their keyed option were repaired. 32 wrong explanations or rule statements (among them several arithmetic errors), 28 unsupported claims, 14 ambiguous cards, 28 unclear ones and 107 minor issues were fixed, and the 60-metre 9.15 W ERP limit was added.
